question: Which reusable proof APIs establish package, browser and raw-device behavior without duplicate inventories?
trigger: The user asked to investigate the new e2e package (tester-army/e2e) and a user report pairing it with pstack verification, evaluate it against the current testing stack including @platejs/test, and cut any prior art it beats, given unit tests that drift from real behavior and no appetite for hours of Playwright suites.
requirements: Catch editor behavior defects that users see, such as caret, IME, selection, focus, paint, mobile input and assistive technology, before a reporter does.

A browser editing claim needs model, DOM and native selection or geometry, focus owner and follow-up typing; model-only proof never certifies browser behavior (VISION.md, docs/vision/common.md claim width).
A raw mobile or device claim needs real device artifacts; a mobile viewport on a desktop engine proves only viewport behavior.
Every test fails for a named, plausible defect; no broad smoke suites or exhaustive matrices; native-risk proof runs five warm times (AGENTS.md Tests rule, verify).
Keep machine and agent time low: no hours-long end-to-end suites.
No outbound message, telemetry report or paid model call without the owner's authorization.
No product implementation in this assessment.
evidenceReuse: First review of the proof scope. New this review: a source read of tester-army/e2e at c6c39ad3 (e2e@0.15.2), of agent-device 0.21.18, argent, stim and MiniSim; an inventory of @platejs/test, the Bun, DOM and Playwright suites, CI and 20 drift cases with 16 device and assistive-technology gates; and a live probe on a local Android emulator with Chrome 146 and Gboard. Reused the 2026-10-02 autocomplete re-challenge's accessibility-tree method and its emulated Android rows.
summary: Pursue a real-device lane inside the existing stack and stop on e2e. The drift comes from stand-ins inside green tests, not from too few end-to-end tests: the browser suites take minutes, while 12 of 20 drift cases went red only in installed or headed Chrome or with real OS input. The harness falls back to the page handle when native paste changes nothing, sends shortcut chords as constructed events, and the mobile projects run desktop engines with phone profiles. e2e cannot close that gap: its agent types with locator.fill, never sees a collapsed caret, has no IME, clipboard or held-key API, refuses URLs on mobile targets, and sends telemetry by default; a Plate integration for it would rebuild @platejs/test behind an agent that still types through fill. The mobile agent tools commit text through their own test keyboard or adb and read no page state. Playwright already reaches Chrome for Android: over adb and CDP it attached to the real page with no flags, real touches drove Gboard, and the existing model oracle read every step, including a correct mention completion from a tapped option. Gboard sent committed insertText per letter with no composition, so the emulated composition the suites assume is not what that keyboard sends. iOS Safari and screen readers stay open with named probes.

callSites.current: Android claims run in the Plite 'mobile' project: devices['Pixel 5'] on desktop Chromium, with await editor.ime.compose({ text: 'biggs' }) sending CDP composition; await editor.clipboard.pasteHtml(html, text) falls back to a synthetic paste event or the page handle when native paste changes nothing.
callSites.proposed: Proposed: const { editor, keyboard } = await openAndroidExample('/blocks/mention-demo') attaches to Chrome on an emulator or device over adb and CDP; await keyboard.type('@biggs') taps soft-keyboard keys with real touches; await editor.assert.modelBlockText(0, '@biggsMention') reads the same oracle. await editor.clipboard.pasteHtml(html, text) fails when native paste changes nothing unless the call passes { transport: 'handle' }, which marks the step as a stand-in.

alternatives: Adopt e2e as the end-to-end layer: rejected. Its agent types through locator.fill, which @platejs/test bans as editor proof; its text view hides a collapsed caret; it has no IME, clipboard or held-key action; mobile targets refuse app.url; cache issues for same-node text changes were closed into a private tracker; telemetry is on by default and its skill tells agents to send feedback reports.

Build a Plate integration for e2e, a wrapper engine with an editor fixture: rejected. It duplicates @platejs/test inside e2e's engine contract and still leaves typing to fill; the replay cache only saves model calls that Plate's agents never make, because they write deterministic Playwright through verify.

Adopt agent-device, argent, stim or MiniSim as the device owner: rejected. agent-device commits text through its own test keyboard by default, argent and MiniSim use adb input text, stim serves only React Native, and none reads page JavaScript in a mobile browser or captures screen-reader speech.

Add a device lane to @platejs/test (selected): Playwright over adb and CDP plus real touches on the soft keyboard, reusing the harness oracle, for tagged Android cases only, run on demand and nightly rather than per pull request; its receipts replace the raw-mobile schema's directAppium requirement with a transport field.

Make stand-ins fail loud (selected): paste without a native effect fails unless the call opts into the handle, constructed shortcut events and handle setters are labeled in the trace, and proof assertions reject labeled steps.

Narrow the emulated mobile projects (selected): keep viewport-tagged cases and move raw-input claims to the device lane, because the Pixel 5 project skipped 387 of 704 rows and models composition that real Gboard did not send.
Borrow e2e's accessibility-tree cross-check as a cheap proxy for popup and focus claims; it never stands in for a screen reader.
Keep the stack unchanged: loses, because 16 device and assistive-technology gates have no producer and the raw-mobile receipt validator has never received a receipt.
proofLimits: The Android lane ran once per step on an emulator, not five warm runs and not a physical phone, with Gboard key positions read from a screenshot. e2e, agent-device, argent, stim and MiniSim were read, not run; no paid model call was made. Drift case counts come from plans and decision logs mined by a subagent with three spot checks. The www suite's duration is unknown. iOS Safari has no page-state reader in any surveyed tool; WebDriver against the simulator is an untested next probe. No screen reader ran. The page handle attaches with read and write methods on every mounted Editable with no environment gate; whether production builds should keep it is not settled here.
